assignments.brief_reason: Explicit fairness rule requiring removal of both parties for balance.
Audience fact-checking/resilience framing doesn’t match the moderation-standard or threat/toxicity themes.
Fairness/balance to both sides is described as the guiding criterion.
Dialogue/civility orientation focuses on avoiding horrible insults (toxicity-like disqualifier).
Point-vs-nonsense decision rule doesn’t clearly map to the violence/threat or toxicity/removal themes.
Treats offensiveness as the key cue for removal, aligning with toxicity filtering.
Reverses from removing hateful content to allowing based on a strong free-speech stance (with no stated violence exception).
Impact assessment per statement is described, but not clearly as pair/mirror comparison that drives decisions.
Two-step check starts with personal insults/uncivil language as a disqualifier (toxicity/civility filtering).
Fairness to both sides plus removal when derogation becomes too derogatory toward a group (toxicity threshold).
Free-speech broadly but rejects only for profanity; closest to speech-allowed with specific “bad language” exception.
Open to free speech with explicit exceptions for violence advocacy and curse words.
Pair-level removal even when one is passable, framed as a fairness/consistent standard applied across both sides.
Defaulting to keeping both due to inability to differentiate within the pair doesn’t fit the codebook themes.
Content quality vs anger/sense is a cue-based rule not covered by the existing moderation/exception themes.
Decides based on how much they agreed with each statement, not mapped to the moderation-standard/threat/toxicity themes.
Uses presence of threat/harm signals as the basis for rejecting content.
Keeps only if coherent and civil; removes if incoherent/inflammatory/bigoted (toxicity/civility filtering).
Disallows foul language as the main keeping/rejecting criterion (toxicity/bad language removal).
Treats profanity/aggression as poor conduct; removal/avoidance aligns with toxicity filtering.
